medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: The Associate Dean for Student Affairs may approve requests for short-term leaves of absence (up to 6 weeks).  Longer leaves of absence must have the approval of the Academic Status Committee.  Leaves of absence usually are classified as "personal," "medical," or "educational."  Requests for leaves of absence should be submitted in writing to the Associate Dean for Student Affairs.  Partial tuition refunds may be possible for medical leaves of absence but not for personal leaves of absence.  During an educational leave of absence (e.g., a research fellowship at the NIH), the student is not registered in the College of Medicine.

medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Gainesville campus lies midway between the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico in the lush beauty of north central Florida. The surrounding area includes fresh water springs, wild prairies, and many parks exhibiting a great diversity of wildlife. Arts and culture abound in Gainesville. The Phillips Center for the Performing Arts features world-class entertainers from all genres. Museums include The Harn Museum of Art and the Florida Museum of Natural History, featuring the McGuire Butterfly Rainforest. Gainesville's many professional Performing Arts groups include the Hippodrome Theatre, Dance Alive National Ballet and The Gainesville Chamber Orchestra, each performing regularly throughout the year.  Gainesville is only an hour and a half from Jacksonville, and two hours from Tampa and Orlando.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Some on-campus housing is available and there are a multitude of affordable apartments within a 5 mile radius.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Wellness initiatives and support are embedded within the UF COM program; these include but are not limited to: the Gator-2-Gator support initiative, numerous events, dedicated fulltime professionals in the areas of counseling and learning support, and faculty mentors who are assigned to each medical student at time of matriculation.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: We believe in taking care of one another and that in this way we can also best learn to care for our patients. Thus  curriculum and campus culture are intertwined. Starting with admissions, we seek those who demonstrate values of collegiality, kindness, humility and collaboration. On interview day, faculty and students lead the programming so that applicants can experience the culture firsthand. First semester, students are placed in small groups mentored by faculty. The groups meet weekly to foster longitudinal connections, team learning and professional identity development. Each new student is also paired with a second year mentor. Peer-teaching is embedded in several courses and P/F grading (years 1 & 2) promotes the goal of group, not only individual success. Each class has both a Service and a Social Chair who bring peers together beyond classroom and clinic. Many other programs encourage connection such as Gator2Gator, Grad Cup (intermurals) and the Medical College Council.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: There is abundant housing close to campus and public bus routes.  Students must be able to travel to preceptorships during first and second year, and clerkships that occasionally require attendance at rural clinics and Jacksonville in the surrounding areas third and fourth year.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students must maintain professional appearance when on the health campus and during any clinical activity or anticipating patient contact. White lab coats should be clean, pressed, and in good repair.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: UF COM is strongly committed to the success of every student. Tutors and a fulltime learning specialist are available. Help is readily offered from course directors, faculty, and fellow students.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Ongoing, beginning with first semester coursework
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Multidisciplinary, including didactic lectures, collaborative learning groups (consisting of 8 students and a dedicated faculty mentor,) problem-based team learning and inter-professional activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin in May following completion of the second year curriculum and Step 1 board exams.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are ranked based on their third year clerkships and required fourth year rotations.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Case-by-case. The vast majority of lectures are video-recorded.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The curriculum at the University of Florida College of Medicine begins and ends with patients. Coursework starts with Genetics and Health followed by the Foundations of Medicine introduction to basic science.  Basic science, human anatomy and clinical medicine are taught in an integrated, cohesive manner; progression is structured by organ system and unified by patients.  Adult learning principles, early and consistent clinical exposure, prioritizing the physician-patient relationship and compassion, honesty/integrity form the basic philosophical underpinnings of our educational program.  In short, we take care of one another, so we can learn, discover and take care of our patients.  In this way, we will educate new physicians who will work hard, think clearly and care deeply.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: All students have the opportunity to participate in clinical and/or basic science research in the College of Medicine and Health Science Center.  The UF HSC is an interdisciplinary research hub, generating more than half of UF's total research awards.  Six health professions colleges, nine major health-related research centers and institutes and multiple affiliate centers offer students abundant research choices and opportunities for synergistic collaboration.  Structured opportunities are offered through the MSRP and Discovery Pathways programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Equal Access Clinic is a free, student-run network of health services for individuals and families in need. Each class also has a Service Chair who coordinates additional community initiatives.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Participation in scholarly activities is strongly encouraged via the Medical Student Research Program program and Discovery Pathways Program.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: UF Health Shands Hospital Gainesville, UF Health Shands Children’s Hospital, UF Health Jacksonville, UF Health Heart & Vascular Hospital, UF Health Neuromedicine Hospital, Malcolm Randall VA Center
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Preclinical years are graded on a pass/fail basis. Clinical rotations are graded on a numeric scale that is assigned a letter grade.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The University of Florida College of Medicine is Florida's oldest public medical school, having admitted its first class in September 1956. Located in the Health Science Center on the 2,000-acre UF campus, the College of Medicine enjoys strong ties with HSC colleges and other university programs. The UF Health Science Center consists of the UF Health Shands Hospital including the Children's Hospital, UF Cancer Hospital and Critical Care Center and UF Health Heart & Vascular Hospital; Stetson Medical Science Building; Harrell Medical Education Building;  Academic Research Building; Health Professions, Nursing and Pharmacy Building; Cancer and Genetics Research Building; McKnight Brain Institute; Veterans Affairs Medical Center; Nanotechnology Center and the Emerging Pathogens Center. UF's Jacksonville Regional Medical Center supports a full spectrum of UF residency training programs.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The UF College of Medicine strives to improve health care in Florida, our nation, and the world through excellence, superior leadership in education, clinical care, discovery, and service.

We advance our mission through a curriculum and learning environment focused on training our students above all to care deeply and well for their patients and for each other. Six core competencies guide the training, assessment and feedback students can expect: medical knowledge, patient care, systems-based practice, professionalism, communication and practice-based guided learning and improvement. Our curriculum organizes the acquisition of medical knowledge and skills using a systems-based approach that integrates basic sciences, clinical sciences, health systems, social sciences, and wellbeing. Faculty nurture students’ professional identity through structured encounters with standardized patients, longitudinal mentorship both individually and in teams and immersion in real world scenarios.  We intend for all of our students to become well-rounded leaders in patient advocacy.

UF Health’s wide service area promotes health systems-informed practice and an interdisciplinary, team-based culture. Students have easy access to mentors and teachers in over 100 primary care, advanced specialty and subspecialty services. In addition, our students learn from and practice with social services professionals, attending faculty, trainees and patients, among other team members, to coordinate care, problem-solve and improve patient outcomes. The full campus in Gainesville includes Shands Hospital, a quaternary care facility which serves as UF’s main teaching hospital and five co-located affiliate hospitals including a Veterans Affairs hospital and children’s hospital, six health professions colleges and ten research centers/institutes. UF Health Jacksonville, now a regional campus for clerkship years, offers a downtown training hospital and multiple inpatient and outpatient practices serving patients throughout North Florida and South Georgia.  We also encourage our students to participate in research and discovery across our academic and clinical enterprises. Eleven scholarly tracks offer short and long term research opportunities.

A program based on care will not succeed without an environment that also cares for students. Robust student services include a full-time counselor, full-time learning specialist, structured peer-to-peer mentoring program, wellness curriculum and multiple mechanisms for students to contribute to ongoing program improvement.

Our mission informs an admissions practice that seeks those who are not only academically accomplished but medically informed and who exhibit throughout the application a genuine drive to learn, work and serve in intra- and interdisciplinary teams. Successful candidates demonstrate a desire to grow and be challenged personally, academically and professionally. In evaluating the application and interview, we credit the myriad ways that individuals acquire and demonstrate the character, preparation, resilience and skills that contribute to transforming good medical students into excellent physicians. We evaluate the competencies we seek in part by asking applicants to reflect on how their personal values intersect with medicine and to attempt to think like a physician by responding to the narrative of a real patient encounter. As our curriculum emphasizes exceptional patient care within a setting that prioritizes community and student support, the personal attributes that applicants demonstrate are key as we consider who will thrive in and enhance our community. We evaluate these in the written application by way of the quality and consistency of essays, experiences, and letters of recommendation.  During the interview phase we conduct one-on-one conversational interviews and incorporate our students and faculty throughout our interview day to introduce future students to our community.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: All letters must be submitted through AMCAS and received no later than January 15 for consideration for entry  the following August.  If offered by the applicant's institution, we will accept one *evaluative* committee letter; we strongly prefer that a committee letter is accompanied by at least two complete individual letters (either appended or uploaded separately), so that the letter section of the application includes three full evaluative letters of recommendation.  Equally acceptable to fulfill the letter requirement is a packet of between 3 - 6 individual letters combined in one document, or 3-6 separate individual letters of recommendation.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: A specific distribution of recommenders is not required; letters of recommendation are a critical aspect of holistic review. Applicants are advised to select recommenders who know them well and can collectively best address the range of competencies in all three categories outlined by the AAMC here: https://www.aamc.org/download/349990/data/lettersguidelinesbrochure.pdf
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Program consists of short presentations and sessions demonstrating the curriculum and student life in the morning, two interviews and a tour in the afternoon.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two partially blind (MCAT and GPA withheld) one-on-one interviews with members of our interview committee.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Synchronous live interviews offered for 2027 interview cycle

medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Must be permanent legal residents of the U.S. U.S. citizens or permanent residents who attend Canadian university are eligible.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
We welcome applications from US citizens and permanent residents who have earned, or will earn by the time of intended matriculation, a bachelor's degree in any field from an accredited US or Canadian 4 year college or university. 

Prerequisite lectures and labs are acceptable regardless of in-person, online or hybrid format.  A letter grade of "C" or higher is required in all prerequisite science courses (or higher level substitute), with the exception of spring and summer 2020 (P/S acceptable). 

Please see our complete admissions requirements here:
https://admissions.med.ufl.edu/admission-requirements/regular-admission-requirements/
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: An applicant's MCAT history is considered as part of a comprehensive review process that balances academic preparation, experience and personal attributes
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: We strongly consider postbacc and graduate science GPAs
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: A strong postbacc or science-based master's GPA will be considered in determining academic readiness for medical school.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We require a bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited post-secondary 4 year college or university in the US or Canada.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept lower division prerequisites taken at community colleges. Biochemistry must be completed at a four year college or university and must be an upper division version of the subject, and approved  to count towards a premedical or science major curriculum at the institution where taken.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Our secondary application portal accepts applicant uploads at any time during the application cycle; we welcome and prefer updates (both academic and extra-curricular) midcycle for those who complete secondaries in summer or early fall.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial assistance is available to all students who show need. Scholarships and low interest loans are available, as well as research fellowships.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: We welcome all majors and academic disciplines. Prerequisite coursework must include an academic year sequence of biology with labs (suitable for a bio science or Pre-Health track) and should include a strong focus on cellular structure and function. In addition we require an academic year sequence of physics (algebra or calc-based) with labs, and an academic year sequence of general chemistry with labs. We recognize that chemistry sequences vary by institution, so for schools that offer only one semester of general chemistry with lab, a second semester of organic chemistry can substitute.  Additionally, we require the first semester of a sequence of organic chemistry, an organic chemistry lab, and a semester of upper level biochemistry (no lab required). The biochemistry cannot be substituted. A letter grade C or higher is required for all prerequisites (except Spring/Sum 2020 when P/S is accepted). Advanced coursework in a discipline can substitute.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We recommend the most advanced science coursework be no older than 5 years from matriculation without current professional competency in the subjects.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: We appraise applicants on academic record, MCAT, personal attributes, activities,  and recommendations. A personal interview is required and is granted at the discretion of the Medical Student Admissions Committee. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, sexual orientation, gender, age, disability, creed or national origin. As a public institution, Florida residents are given preference. However, well qualified non-residents are considered,  particularly those who have a record of service and ties to Florida.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Substantial experience in the medical field, preferably including a combination of shadowing and interaction with patients, is desirable.  Medical experience considered can encompass volunteering, observing/shadowing, clinical research and/or clinical employment.
